problem: Dual-system VLN methods hand guidance from the slow VLM to the fast planner only after VLM reasoning finishes, so the planner acts on stale guidance in dynamic scenes. Static, blocking VLN benchmarks also hide this observation staleness.
motivation: In human-populated spaces a maneuver chosen at inference start can become a proxemic violation or collision by the time it executes. The authors observe that a VLM's intermediate-token hidden states already encode directional intent and pedestrian context long before generation ends, so the bottleneck is delivery of guidance rather than the reasoning itself.
key_idea: Stream the slow VLM's per-token intermediate hidden states, compressed into fixed-size latent slots, to a fast flow-matching planner throughout generation, so the planner is conditioned on evolving guidance instead of a single end-of-reasoning latent.
insight: The gain comes from delivery timing and from how the stream is aggregated. Wait-then-Act with the same VLM and planner reaches 24.80 SR versus 34.80 SR for streaming in the Realistic environment, and mean-pooling the stream drops SR to 25.20 versus 34.80 for cross-attention. Streaming cuts effective latency from 0.788 s to 0.185 s and average pedestrian displacement per inference from 0.213 m to 0.050 m, which is the mechanism behind reduced staleness.
method: Token-Wise Hidden Streamer: during autoregressive VLM decoding (VILA-8B, frozen), collects hidden states from layers 16-23 at every generated token, forming a growing stream H in R^{L x k_t x D}.

Sequence-to-Slot Latent Bridge: adds learnable layer and time positional encodings, projects D to the planner dimension d, and compresses the stream with Perceiver-style multi-head cross-attention from N=8 learnable queries plus an FFN, giving fixed-size latent slots R_t.

Evolving Latent Conditioner: the planner condition is [z_obs; z_goal], where z_goal is the streamed slots R_t for language goals (a linear-projected point goal for PointNav, none for no-goal); slots are recomputed as tokens arrive and the planner re-plans.

Flow-matching expert planner: a transformer vector field trained with a rectified-flow loss, decoding H waypoints with 5-step Euler integration and sampling N_c candidate trajectories. It is pretrained on point-goal navigation (Ours-S1) and adapted to VLN by adding the slots, with goal coordinate set to zero.
Goal-agnostic safety critic: an ESDF-supervised critic scores candidates for collision-freeness and smoothness from the observation tokens and selects the executed trajectory.

Dynamic social VLN benchmark: Idealized (simulator pauses during inference) and Realistic (non-blocking; pedestrians move during inference) stages, with ORCA goal-directed pedestrians, density scaled to scene area, and encounter patterns (frontal, intersection, following, corner). Metrics: SR, NE, SPL, PSC, Col, AvgD, plus latency and displacement statistics.

setting.backbone: VILA-8B VLM reasoner (frozen) + flow-matching expert planner and Sequence-to-Slot bridge (trained)
setting.training_data: Planner pretrained on point-goal navigation data; bridge and planner adapted for VLN with streamed slots. Training data scale is not specified in the text.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (planner); 8 recent egocentric RGB frames plus instruction (VLM)
setting.action_space: continuous trajectory of H waypoints (x,y,yaw) from rectified flow matching, selected by a safety critic
setting.simulator: custom dynamic social simulator with ORCA pedestrians (simulator not named in the text)

numbers_note: The paper gives no split name for its own benchmark; 'test' is used as a placeholder. No results on standard benchmarks such as R2R-CE.
results: On the proposed dynamic social VLN benchmark, SPARK-VLN reaches 41.60 SR in the Idealized environment (vs NaVILA 37.20, DualVLN 26.20) and 34.80 SR / 28.68 SPL in the Realistic environment (vs Uni-NaVid 30.20 SR, NaVILA 29.00, DualVLN 22.90), with the lowest collision rate there (29.3). The planner alone beats NavDP on PointNav (70.7 vs 61.1 SR Idealized; 61.2 vs 53.2 Realistic).
limitations: Absolute VLN success is low (34.8-41.6 SR) and evaluation is only on the authors' own simulated benchmark; no standard VLN benchmarks or real-robot tests.
Handles short single-goal instructions only; longer multi-sub-goal instructions and pedestrian intent prediction are left to future work.
The planner receives no goal coordinate in VLN, so it depends entirely on the language slots; the streamed latents are not shown to be semantically faithful before the answer is complete.
